root_cause_label: Heuristic-Based Motion Peak Thresholds Produce Frame Numbers Outside Ground-Truth Range
one_sentence_failure_summary: The agent repeatedly designed and iterated on motion-percentage heuristics anchored to an arbitrary peak-motion threshold rather than deriving kinematic features aligned with the ground-truth definitions of takeoff and landing, producing final frame numbers (110, 117) far outside the benchmark-expected range.
t_err_evidence: Script created with `from scipy.signal import find_peaks`, a forbidden third-party import violating allowed-dependency constraints.
t_commit_evidence: Step 24: once the heuristic algorithm is committed to (background-subtraction motion % + peak-anchored thresholds), all subsequent iterations remain in this conceptual frame. Despite 50+ more steps of refinement, the agent never switches to a fundamentally different approach (e.g., vertical-position tracking via contour centroids), so the failure is locked in at the moment of initial algorithm commitment.
t_surface_evidence: Script runs at step 27 with exit code 0 but produces incorrect frame numbers (107/118) rather than failing explicitly on the forbidden import.
trigger_explanation: The agent acts on the unverified assumption that the peak of frame-to-frame (or background-subtracted) motion percentage directly corresponds to the jump apex, and that fixed percentage-of-peak thresholds (20% for takeoff, 70% for landing) will correctly identify biomechanical takeoff and landing frames. This assumption is never verified against ground-truth definitions, yet drives all subsequent design choices.
